- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially after sharp drops.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use mean reversion.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 74→70→68), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias in 3–7 day horizon.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model may lag; adjust forecast downward 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- For 30-day forecasts, if history shows volatility >10% over 5 days, model tends to smooth too much; add 1–2% upward bias to account for volatility.
